activity_page.section1_title: How to Live and Learn on Campus
activity_page.section1_description: First steps to university life: learn to live and live to learn. Including learning to adapt to new environments that require independent thinking, as well as being able to find information, communicate, and solve problems with others. It is ready to work with others.
activity_page.section1_point1: How to Live is learning to live in university, adapting to the university, and living life, including learning to adapt to new environments that require independent thinking, including being able to find information, communicate, and solve problems with others. Ready to work with others.
activity_page.section1_point2: How to Learn is To enhance your academic and personal growth, it’s essential to actively engage with the student association in your faculty. This can provide valuable insights into academic resources, activities, and student-led initiatives. Communicate regularly with friends in your own faculty, other faculties, and your department to broaden your perspective, share knowledge, and build supportive networks. Learn from departmental activities, major and elective subjects, and explore relevant information from sub-departments to gain a deeper understanding of your field. Additionally, stay curious about research developments by following updated research data, which helps you stay current and academically competitive.
activity_page.section2_title: United Spirit: Flag Contest among Academic Schools
activity_page.section2_description: This activity is designed for first-year students from each academic school to showcase their unity and school spirit by performing the MFU (Mae Fah Luang University) March, which they have practiced thoroughly. The goal is to deliver a performance that is harmonious, powerful, and full of energy. Once all flags from each school are collected, it signifies the successful completion of the university-wide flag contest. At that moment, all first-year students will come together to sing the Mae Fah Luang University March and chant the university cheer in unison, marking the official conclusion of the activity.
activity_page.section3_description: This activity continues the royal initiative of Her Royal Highness Princess Srinagarindra, and has become a cherished tradition for Mae Fah Luang University freshmen. New students come together to participate in a reforestation effort as a symbol of environmental responsibility and unity. The event is supported by the university’s Botanical Garden, which provides five species of saplings: Indian Gooseberry (Phyllanthus emblica), Golden Tectona (Tectona grandis), Teak (Tectona grandis), Yangna (Dipterocarpus alatus), and Couroupita guianensis (Kham Mok Luang), along with Shorea roxburghii (Payom).
activity_page.section4_title: First Date: IT School CE & DCE
activity_page.section4_description: To warmly welcome new students of the Computer Engineering (CE) and Digital and Communication Engineering (DCE) programs into the IT School family, senior students from Year 2, Year 3, and Year 4 organized this heartfelt activity. The event featured introductions to senior students, a welcoming ceremony, and the participation of faculty members from the School of Information Technology. One of the key highlights was the introduction of the student “lineage” system, which fosters connection across academic years. This meaningful event marked the return of a beloved tradition that had been paused due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
activity_page.section5_description: This activity promotes unity, sportsmanship, and mutual respect among students within the programs and the School of Information Technology through various friendly competitions. Events include football, basketball, cheer stand contests, and traditional Thai games. Each activity emphasizes teamwork, strategic planning, and collective effort — all essential elements in working together toward a common goal in a spirited and harmonious atmosphere.
activity_page.section6_description: This ceremony warmly welcomes new students in the engineering program and celebrates their entry into the field through the symbolic presentation of the Engineering Practical Shirt. It also serves as a meaningful opportunity for students to connect with faculty members and senior peers, fostering strong bonds within the department. The event provides a space for new students to ask questions and seek guidance regarding their studies and future career paths — laying the foundation for collaboration, mentorship, and a lasting sense of professional community.
activity_page.section7_title: Polo Shirt Design Contest – Computer Engineering Program
activity_page.section7_description: This special occasion invites all 1st, 2nd and 3rd year Computer Engineering students to showcase their creativity and design skills by designing the official polo shirt for the program. The shirt design not only reflects the identity of the program but also symbolizes unity among students. This collaboration helps promote pride, belonging and professional relationships within the Computer Engineering field.

my_works_page.description: My Works & Projects : Nonstop Learning in the Tech World
my_works_page.description1: Starting a project today is not just about completing a task—it is about preparing myself to adapt, solve problems, and grow alongside the rapid changes in the digital world. My journey in technology is not just about acquiring knowledge; it is about applying it in meaningful ways to create impactful solutions.
my_works_page.project1_title: Estimation of obesity levels based on eating habits and physical condition Model
my_works_page.project1_details: It was created to examine and measure obesity levels by considering eating behavior and physical condition, using the RapidMiner program, a modern technology for studying and analyzing the received data.
my_works_page.project2_details: Design a network connection across routers, including subnetting, IP addressing, default gateways, VLAN configurations, trunks, and inter-VLAN routing. The goal is to ensure seamless communication and successful pinging between devices.
my_works_page.project3_details: I design websites using Figma and develop them with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, defining roles for User, Admin, and Approver. I also manage databases with XAMPP to ensure smooth system functionality.
my_works_page.project4_title: Project Humidity and Wirelessly & Turn on and offlights System (PM)
my_works_page.project4_description: Embedded System and Internet of Things
my_works_page.project4_details: Develop a soil moisture monitoring system that triggers a LED alert when the moisture level reaches a predefined threshold. The system sends data from the board via the internet to Node-RED, which displays the moisture status on a dashboard.
my_works_page.project5_details: Implement object detection with Faster R-CNN to classify predefined objects by name or confidence, using a pre-trained model for localization, detection, and testing with uploaded images.
my_works_page.project6_details: Design a meeting room booking application using Figma for the UI, defining roles for User, Admin, and Approver. Develop the system with Dart and Flutter, integrating a database via XAMPP for data management.
my_works_page.project7_details: This project involved the complete design and implementation of a car booking system with a focus on database architecture. I began by designing an efficient relational database schema to manage car details, booking records, user accounts, and administrator roles. The database ensures data integrity, supports complex queries, and provides real-time updates.To complement the database, I developed a simple yet functional web interface that allows users to view available cars, make bookings, and check booking statuses. Admins can manage car availability and oversee all bookings. The frontend communicates with the backend using PHP and MySQL via XAMPP, ensuring a smooth and reliable data exchange process.
my_works_page.project8_title: Analysis and simulation of energy improvement in power systems
my_works_page.project8_details: This project involves analyzing and simulating electrical power systems to improve energy efficiency, focusing on power factor correction. It studies the role of reactive power and the negative effects of low power factor on system performance, such as increased energy losses and reduced system stability.The simulation tests various scenarios to observe the impact of reactive power on voltage regulation, current flow, and energy consumption. The project explores possible solutions, including the installation of capacitor banks and synchronous condensers, to compensate for reactive power.Reducing reactive power through these methods helps increase the efficiency of active power usage, decrease energy losses, and enhance the stability and reliability of the electrical system.
my_works_page.project9_title: Network design and configuration with OSPF, BGP and MPLS
my_works_page.project9_details: Designed and simulated a service provider-level network using GNS3, implementing OSPF for internal routing, and both eBGP and iBGP for inter-AS communication. MPLS was configured to enhance data forwarding efficiency and support advanced features such as VPN and traffic engineering.This project focuses on building a scalable and efficient network architecture that mimics real-world ISP environments. It strengthens skills in network design, protocol configuration, and troubleshooting in complex multi-AS systems, providing hands-on experience with enterprise-grade networking technologies.
my_works_page.project10_details: This project focuses on developing a learning kit and step-by-step laboratory exercises to introduce users to the basics of Home Assistant and IoT systems. It is designed specifically for beginners, including high school students, university students, and enthusiasts with little or no background in the field.The learning kit includes carefully designed lessons and activities that guide learners from basic setup to practical use, allowing them to gain hands-on experience with sensors, automation, and smart home integration. Each lab encourages exploration and experimentation, helping users understand how smart devices communicate and operate within the Home Assistant platform.The goal of the project is to make IoT education more accessible by offering clear, beginner-friendly materials that can be used for self-learning, classrooms, or workshops, empowering users to build real-world IoT solutions with confidence.
